newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela sets 100 bln bolivar TEM auction Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela sets 100 bln bolivar TEM auction Tuesday.

text.p: The Central Bank of Venezuela announced for Tuesday morning a 60 billion bolivar ($127 million) auction of 180-day "monetary stabilization," or TEM, bills with a 14.63 percent coupon.
The bank said it would also offer 20 billion bolivars ($42 million) in 269-day bills with a 14.89 percent coupon, and another 20 billion bolivars of 358-day bills with a 15.16 percent coupon.
Forty-two billion boivars of TEMs are due to mature on Thursday.

Coupons at the Tuesday auction are down from last week's 80 billion bolivar issue when 179-, 268- and 358-day notes carried 14.99, 15.27, and 15.55 percent coupons respectively for effective yields that softened slightly to 14.63, 19.56 and 21.56 percent.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
